definitions.note: read as 'Primate is', the 's standing for 'is'

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so one letter is dropped from the word for weariness

O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A remark about a tired ape gasping for air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes the O from LANGUOR. The 's of 'Primate's' is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The langur is a long-tailed Asian monkey, a member of the primate order.

clue.text: Go for a time on a different course

parts.note: taken as written
to tack is to change a sailing boat's course, and a tack is such a new heading

explanation.surface: Advice to take a new route and try again.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for someone is to assault them, a common idiomatic synonym.

parts.note: literally cigars burn away to ash and fumes; figuratively the phrase means plans come to nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes to nothing is said to vanish like smoke, an idiom for being wasted.

clue.text: Reader, I married him in Kentish Town

definitions.meaning: the famous line in Jane Eyre, spoken of the brooding master of Thornfield
a cathedral city in the English county of Kent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Kentish Town' is also a district of London, which is the misdirection; here it means a town in Kent. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre's husband is Mr Edward Fairfax of that surname, which is also the name of a Kent town.

indicators.note: something spoken of is said out loud, so the writer's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Thomas Carlyle was the Scottish essayist and historian

explanation.surface: A town said to be named for a Scottish author.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlisle is a cathedral city in Cumbria, near the Scottish border.

clue.text: Plant has lost a lot of time

indicators.note: a word that has lost something no longer contains it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: centaury is a small flowering plant of the gentian family

explanation.surface: A gardener lamenting that a plant has taken ages to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost' removes the A from CENTAURY.
explanation.definitionFit: A century is a hundred years, which is certainly a long stretch of time.

clue.text: Root up and show as bad

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tuber is a swollen root such as a potato

explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TUBER round to give the answer, since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut an argument is to refute it, showing it to be false or unsound.

indicators.note: not means without here, so the letter for following is taken away

parts.note: fire is ardour or passionate feeling
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger, a strong emotion of the kind once called a passion.

clue.text: In books, it rarely needs editing

indicators.note: text that needs editing will be rearranged, so the letters of the words before are reordered

explanation.surface: A comment that a word seldom requires an editor's attention in print.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary means relating to books and written works, so in books it is at home.

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Mythical horse-men wandering the Italian countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Etruscan describes ancient Etruria, a region of central Italy, and its people.

definitions.meaning: in grammar the voice of a verb is either this or passive
a volcano still liable to erupt is described this way, as opposed to dormant

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the words alongside are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A complaint that a long-running process keeps going wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unfavourable or inconvenient, a close synonym of adverse.

clue.text: Craftsman we will fix up by phone

indicators.note: heard by phone, words are taken by sound, not spelling

parts.note: we will is contracted to we'll, and fix up gives right, as in right a wrong

explanation.surface: A tradesman promising a customer on the phone that the job will be sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: WE'LL sounds like WHEEL and RIGHT like WRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelwright is a craftsman who builds and repairs wooden wheels.

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning to stir up quarrelling
playfully, a device placed by the ears

explanation.definitionFit: To set people by the ears is an old idiom meaning to make them quarrel.

clue.text: Journalist looked after new pedestrian R MAGN

indicators.note: after places the word for looked behind the letter for new

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, especially a jobbing one
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A reporter keeping an eye on a fresh walker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looked after' reads as cared for, but 'after' puts EYED after N.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian in the sense of dull and uninspired matches hackneyed, meaning trite.

clue.text: Lightly touch my rear in diffident com- 09015 622 passion

parts.note: shy means diffident

parts.note: taken as written before turning
to pat is to touch lightly

explanation.surface: Comforting a shy person with a gentle pat on the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear' works as 'raise up', turning the short word in this down clue; the digits splitting 'compassion' are stray print on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Sympathy is fellow feeling for another's suffering, the same as compassion.

parts.note: hypo is sodium thiosulphate, the fixer used in developing photographs
critical means fault-finding

explanation.surface: A dishonest repairer who complains about everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypocritical means insincere or two-faced, close in sense to fraudulent.

clue.text: Not that the lady inside is a robber

indicators.note: inside puts the lady within the word for not that

parts.note: this is the opposite of that
Eve, the first lady in Genesis

explanation.surface: A remark that a woman indoors is a burglar.
explanation.definitionFit: To thieve is to steal, so one who thieves is acting as a robber.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the law wraps round the knight

parts.note: a canon is a law or rule, especially of the church
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A legal rule concerning a knight's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large gun, a type of artillery weapon.

clue.text: As social activity, a lot of reporters attend The King and!

parts.note: taken as written
the press is reporters collectively
K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: Journalists going en masse to see the musical The King and I.
explanation.walkthrough: The King and I is a stage musical. 'As' and 'attend' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising enjoyed after a day on the slopes.

parts.note: Pierre is the capital of South Dakota, abbreviated SD
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.definitionFit: To while away time is to spend it idly.

explanation.surface: Someone confessing they mistreat their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire means clothing, a collective word for garments.

parts.note: continuing the previous clue, this names a mishap that befalls someone else

explanation.definitionFit: Ill as a noun means harm or misfortune, as in an ill wind.

an ad is a bill, a poster advertisement

explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclades are a group of Greek islands in the Aegean Sea.
